source_caption:
During the tense sequence on Miller’s planet—where the crew is threatened by massive, mountain-sized tidal waves—composer Hans Zimmer’s track “Mountains” features a distinct, rhythmic ticking sound in the background. Because the ocean planet is situated incredibly close to the supermassive black hole Gargantua, it experiences extreme gravitational time dilation where one hour on the surface equals seven years on Earth. The ticking in Zimmer’s score occurs exactly every 1.25 seconds, which, when calculated against the film’s time-slippage ratio, means that every single audible “tick” represents an entire day passing back home on Earth. This brilliant piece of auditory design subtly reinforces the devastating, ticking-clock stakes of the mission without a single line of exposition.

Interstellar (2014), directed by Christopher Nolan, starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Michael Caine. As Earth faces a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl that threatens humanity’s survival, a team of astronauts travels through a newly discovered wormhole in search of a habitable new home, battling devastating forces of relativity and time along the way.

source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
